Even having gone through cognitive behavioral therapy and taking medication, there are still days where I feel depressed. They happen more often than I like to admit. I don’t have any motivation to do my work, eat, or socialize.

As I was getting older and approaching middle school, I was caught up in a hurricane of emotions. The influx of hormones from puberty, struggling with my own self-image, and trying to find friends, all led me to spiral more into a depression.
There was a lot going on in my life that my therapist and I have speculated could have contributed to me becoming more depressed and struggling. I remember thinking that I had to hold in my emotions.

When I was 18 years old, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and general anxiety. I have always struggled with some form of depression growing up, and I can trace back similar symptoms since I was 11 years old. I would hide myself away from others and become very quiet.
